title: Signal
description: A computed signal with its window, confidence, and permitted uses — the runtime instance of docs/data/metric-definitions.md. 'mayDrive' is machine-enforced: a policy that consumes a signal for a channel the signal is not allowed to drive fails validation, which is how 'ACWR is display-only' stays true after we forget why.

key.description: Registry key from metric-definitions.md. Adding a key requires a definition there first. These strings are copied verbatim from the metric registry, so they keep that namespace's spelling rather than this contract's kebab-case rule; tools must not rewrite them.

asOfDay.description: Training day the signal describes (inclusive end of its window).

window.description: Part of the metric's identity: acwr(7/28) and acwr(28/28) are different metrics that happen to share a name.

value.description: null is a real answer: we prefer an honest null to a guessed number (metric-definitions.md rule 1).

unit.description: AU · bpm · sec/km · % · score. Never inferred downstream.

baselineValue.description: The user's own baseline for deviation-type signals; never a population average.

confidence.description: Computed as the minimum confidence of the inputs, never the maximum.

confidenceNote.description: Surfaced in reviews: 'no HR data on 2 of 4 sessions' is what makes a verdict believable.

mayDrive.description: Allowed consumers. Display-only metrics carry ['display'] and any policy that reads them for another channel is rejected.

consecutiveDays.description: Supports the 3-consecutive-reading rule for HRV/RHR without re-scanning history.

crossedThreshold.description: Set by the hysteresis pair (metric-definitions.md rule 3), so a signal that flaps around its cut does not flap the policy.

source.description: 'assumed' means filled by a documented default (e.g. load_sRPE with RPE 5 when RPE is missing) and is always labelled.

exclusions.description: e.g. 'non-representative: 1200 km travel day' — excluded from baselines, retained in history.

formulaVersion.description: Which definition produced this value; lets us recompute selectively after a metric change.
